item.title: Pay for 10 litres, get less: Fuel theft persists despite raids
item.description:
Motorists in Dhaka are being shortchanged at filling stations through manipulated fuel dispensers, with a recent government inspection finding that customers received 530 millilitres less fuel for every 10 litres purchased.
The finding at a Sayedabad filling station has exposed a problem that repeated inspections and fines have failed to eliminate.
Consumers across the capital allege even greater losses, sometimes receiving as much as one litre less than the quantity shown on the pump.
Officials say some operators manipulate dispensing equipment so that the meter records more fuel than actually reaches the customer’s vehicle, making the shortage difficult to detect.
BSTI Executive Magistrate Md Mahbubul Islam told Dhaka Tribune on Tuesday that inspectors recently uncovered a 530ml shortage per 10 litres at Ms Pouro Filling Station in Sayedabad.
The station was fined Tk3 lakh.
“Our operations have revealed that fuel theft occurs at filling stations of all sizes across the capital,” he said, adding that customers often have little way of detecting the manipulation.
The problem is not confined to Sayedabad.
Consumers have reported suspected shortages at pumps in Badda, Rayer Bazar, Sat Rasta and other areas of Dhaka.
BSTI has previously taken enforcement action against several stations, including Mecca Filling Station in Badda and City Filling Station at Sat Rasta, imposing fines ranging from Tk50,000 to Tk3 lakh.
Yet complaints continue.
Officials from the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP) said some fuel dispensers are fitted with electronic chips or remote-controlled circuits that interfere with measurements.
The display may show the correct quantity and price while the amount delivered is lower.
Officials also described instances in which attendants repeatedly engage and release the nozzle lever during refuelling, allegedly interrupting fuel delivery while the meter continues registering a sale.
Other suspected practices include manipulating dispensing speed and adulterating fuel with cheaper substances.
The authorities have not established that every filling station uses these methods, but officials say the techniques make fraud difficult for ordinary customers to identify.
Ashraful Islam, a City Bank employee who regularly refuels his car and motorcycle in Rayer Bazar, said he began suspecting irregularities after comparing fuel purchases with the distances his vehicles travelled.
He estimated that on some occasions he received nearly one litre less for every 10 litres purchased.
When he later tried to buy fuel in two five-litre containers to check the quantity, station employees refused, he alleged.
His calculations and allegations have not been independently verified.
Mizanur Rahman, a Badda resident, described similar suspicions, claiming that customers sometimes lose half a litre or more from a 10-litre purchase.
“Although authorities have previously conducted raids and imposed fines, the theft persists,” he said.
Long-distance transport operators may face particularly large losses because buses frequently purchase 100 to 200 litres at a time.
Alamgir Mia, a driver of a Hanif air-conditioned bus, said drivers often refuel at night and have limited opportunities to challenge suspected shortages.
BSTI magistrate Mahbubul Islam said some operators exploit the absence of regular night-time enforcement.
A relatively small shortage per litre can add up to a substantial loss when a bus purchases a large volume of fuel.
At the shortage rate BSTI detected in Sayedabad, a customer buying 200 litres would receive 10.6 litres less than paid for, assuming the same rate of under-delivery throughout the transaction.
Bangladesh Petrol Pump Owners Association President Mohammad Nazmul Haque acknowledged that fuel theft remained a problem despite government inspections.
“We have informed the government about the fuel theft. The government has entrusted BSTI with the responsibility of oversight. While BSTI is conducting raids, they have failed to stop the theft,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
He said the association had offered to cooperate with regulators but had not been adequately involved.
According to Nazmul, a committee formed seven or eight years ago to tackle irregularities had produced little practical result.
He demanded stronger action to end the practice.
Energy expert Prof Dr M Shamsul Alam said occasional raids and financial penalties were insufficient to deter fraudulent operators.
He called for the cancellation of licences and criminal prosecution where deliberate fuel theft is established.
Alam also warned that adulterated fuel posed an additional risk to consumers and vehicles.
He urged the authorities to take sustained action against offending stations rather than rely on isolated enforcement drives.
For consumers, the difficulty is that the displayed reading often provides their only immediate assurance of how much fuel they have purchased.
Until regulators can reliably detect manipulation and prevent repeat offences, drivers may continue paying for fuel they never receive.

item.title: Tarique-Takaichi meeting in Tokyo sets out broad agenda for cooperation
item.description:
Bangladesh and Japan have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening their longstanding friendship and expanding economic and strategic cooperation, with Prime Ministers Tarique Rahman and Sanae Takaichi highlighting opportunities in energy security, infrastructure, information technology, trade, investment, technology transfer and regional security.
The two leaders also discussed plans to mobilise 1 trillion Japanese yen, equivalent to approximately $6.3 billion, in private investment in Bangladesh’s energy, infrastructure and information and communication technology (ICT) sectors. Expediting a Japanese delegation’s visit to Bangladesh to advance the investment plan was a key focus of the discussions.
According to state-run news agency BSS, the bilateral summit was held at the Japanese prime minister’s office, known as the Kantei, in Tokyo on Tuesday. The talks focused on deepening bilateral ties and translating shared priorities into concrete initiatives.
At a joint press conference after the meeting, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said the two countries were committed to expanding cooperation in energy, ICT, railways, infrastructure, deep-sea ports and foreign direct investment (FDI).
He announced that several memorandums of understanding (MoUs) would be exchanged during his visit, adding that the outcomes of the talks and shared priorities would be reflected in a joint statement.
Emphasising the need to make bilateral ties a driver of economic growth, job creation and shared prosperity, Tarique invited Japanese investors, businesses and financial institutions to explore investment opportunities in Bangladesh.
He said his government was committed to unlocking Bangladesh’s economic potential through productive investment, technology transfer, skilled employment and mutually beneficial business ventures with Japanese partners.
Energy security featured prominently in the discussions. Tarique said reliable and affordable energy supplies were essential to sustaining economic growth. Thanking Japan for its longstanding support, he called for greater Japanese investment in Bangladesh’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, efficient power generation and renewable energy sectors.
He also referred to a recent 50 billion yen emergency support loan under the Partnership for Power Asia initiative, aimed at strengthening energy security across Asia.
The government considers expanded cooperation in the sector vital to Bangladesh’s industrialisation, increased production and efforts to attract investment.
The prime minister outlined Bangladesh’s long-term infrastructure ambitions, including plans to develop a high-speed rail network connecting six major divisional cities and build elevated roads across the country.
He sought Japanese assistance with planning, technical support, investment and financing for the projects, saying Japan’s experience could help Bangladesh develop modern, integrated transport infrastructure.
The two sides also discussed expanding cooperation in deep-sea port development, railway connectivity and other major infrastructure projects. The initiatives could improve freight transportation and regional connectivity while supporting industrialisation and attracting investment.
As part of efforts to build a technology-driven economy, Tarique proposed establishing a Bangladesh-Japan Tech Park to connect Japanese companies, universities and investors with Bangladesh’s young talent, entrepreneurs and skilled technology workforce.
He proposed prioritising artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, robotics and electronics manufacturing. He also expressed interest in expanding cooperation with Japan in space science, satellite engineering and related technologies, areas in which Japan has advanced capabilities.
The government aims to position Bangladesh as a hub for economic activity, technology and manufacturing. Tarique said Bangladesh could become the world’s ninth-largest consumer economy by 2030, while its gross domestic product (GDP) could exceed $1 trillion by 2034.
He urged Japanese public- and private-sector stakeholders to engage more actively in helping Bangladesh realise its economic potential.
The talks also focused on strengthening commercial ties and expanding Japanese investment in Bangladesh.
Tarique expressed hope that the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) would be implemented swiftly, urging both sides to work together to ensure its benefits reached people in both countries.
He pledged to improve Bangladesh’s business environment by enhancing transparency, predictability and efficiency in regulatory procedures, tax policy, customs clearance and fund transfers.
The prime minister reiterated his government’s commitment to strengthening economic ties through productive investment, technology transfer and skilled job creation.
On the first day of his visit, Tarique met Masumi Kakinoki, chairman of Japanese trading house Marubeni Corporation. Their discussions covered expanding trade and investment, implementing the EPA, and potential Japanese investment in information technology, energy and advanced manufacturing.
The modernisation of Karnaphuli Fertilizer Company Limited (KAFCO) and the possibility of establishing a second fertiliser factory in Bangladesh were also discussed.
Tarique separately met Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) President Akihiko Tanaka to discuss accelerating ongoing development projects, continuing cooperation in infrastructure and economic development, and establishing a Bangladesh-Japan skills partnership.
The proposal to establish a technology village and an innovation city also featured in the discussions. Agricultural modernisation, agro-processing, light engineering and energy security were among the other priority areas.
On Tuesday, the prime minister visited the Nittsu Logistics Hub in Ichikawa, Chiba Prefecture, to learn about Japan’s experience in logistics and supply chain management.
The two prime ministers reaffirmed their commitment to advancing the Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B), a key pillar of Bangladesh-Japan economic cooperation.
In a post on her official social media account, Takaichi said the two countries planned to elevate the initiative into a new strategic cooperation framework called “Sharing Prosperity BIG-B”.
Takaichi described Bangladesh as a friendly country that shared common values with Japan, including democracy and the rule of law. She said Japan would strongly support the nation-building efforts of Tarique’s government, which was formed through a democratic election.
She also highlighted Bangladesh’s strategic geographical position linking South and Southeast Asia and its market of 170 million people as important factors for Japan’s economy.
Takaichi expressed her determination to strengthen the strategic partnership through initiatives involving both governments and private-sector stakeholders. She also said she looked forward to working closely with Tarique to advance peace, stability and shared prosperity in the Indo-Pacific region.
During the meeting, Tarique proposed establishing a joint ministerial commission to identify priority areas, review progress in implementing decisions and turn cooperation opportunities into practical initiatives.
He stressed the importance of stronger engagement between the two countries’ business communities and invited Takaichi to visit Bangladesh at a mutually convenient time.
Alongside bilateral economic cooperation, the two leaders discussed regional and international issues.
Tarique said a lasting solution to the Rohingya crisis lay in Myanmar, emphasising the need for the voluntary, safe, dignified and early repatriation of Rohingyas forcibly displaced from Myanmar’s Rakhine State and now sheltered in Bangladesh.
Expressing deep concern over the deteriorating situation in Myanmar and the resulting displacement crisis, he called for an end to all forms of violence, unhindered humanitarian assistance and dialogue among all relevant parties.
He appreciated Japan’s support for Bangladesh’s humanitarian efforts for the Rohingya and urged Tokyo to remain actively engaged with all stakeholders to help establish peace and stability in Rakhine State.
The two leaders also discussed the United Nations, the Indo-Pacific region, international law and multilateral cooperation.
Tarique reiterated their shared vision of a free, open, peaceful and inclusive Indo-Pacific, stressing the importance of closer cooperation to promote regional connectivity, the free flow of trade and economic growth.
He thanked Japan for supporting Bangladesh Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman’s election as president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
The prime minister also expressed hope that Bangladesh and Japan would work more closely to strengthen multilateral cooperation and address global challenges.
Japan was among the countries that recognised Bangladesh shortly after its independence. For more than three decades, it has remained one of Bangladesh’s most important development partners, contributing to infrastructure development and socioeconomic progress.
Tarique said bilateral relations had been built on mutual respect, trust and a shared commitment to peace, prosperity and stability.
He recalled his father, Ziaur Rahman’s, two visits to Japan and the contributions of his mother, former prime minister Khaleda Zia, to strengthening Bangladesh-Japan relations.
He pledged to follow in their footsteps and take bilateral ties to new heights.
Takaichi also highlighted the longstanding friendship between the two countries and expressed her commitment to deepening cooperation in the years ahead.
Both leaders noted that the partnership could deliver greater benefits if government-level agreements were complemented by stronger private investment, technology transfer, skills development and business-to-business engagement.
Tarique arrived in Tokyo on Monday morning for a four-day official visit at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. He was received at Narita International Airport by Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone.
Yesterday, Tarique received a ceremonial welcome at the Kantei. A contingent of Japan’s armed forces presented a guard of honour, and the national anthems of both countries were played. The two leaders then introduced members of their respective delegations before beginning bilateral talks.
Following the meeting and joint press conference, Takaichi hosted a luncheon in Tarique’s honour at the prime minister’s office. Tarique’s wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, was also present.
On the first day of the visit, Tarique met a high-level parliamentary delegation led by former Japanese prime minister Taro Aso. Acknowledging Aso’s contribution to strengthening bilateral relations, Tarique invited him to visit Bangladesh.
The prime minister also held separate meetings with senior officials of Marubeni Corporation and JICA that day.
The visit marks Tarique’s first trip to Japan since assuming office as prime minister. A key objective is to transform the longstanding friendship between the two countries into a more substantive economic partnership.
Alongside expanding cooperation in energy, infrastructure, technology, trade and investment, the visit has focused on strengthening coordination on regional and international issues.
The Tokyo summit has produced several proposals and commitments that could shape the future of Bangladesh-Japan relations. Whether these translate into tangible economic gains and employment opportunities for Bangladesh will depend on the pace of implementation, progress on the proposed investment plan, the effective execution of the MoUs and the establishment of the proposed joint commission.

item.title: 300 discs, two names, a 14-year murder mystery
item.description:
More than 14 years after journalists Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi were murdered in their Dhaka apartment, investigators have reported potentially significant new leads involving former military officer Ziaul Ahsan and cultural personality Rokeya Prachy, prompting the High Court to seek a direct explanation from an International Crimes Tribunal prosecutor.
The information emerged during a separate investigation by the tribunal and includes digital materials reportedly recovered from Ziaul’s residence in Barisal.
Of approximately 300 discs obtained by investigators, only 90 have so far been examined, according to a progress report presented to the High Court on Tuesday.
The findings have not been independently verified by the task force investigating the double murder, and no conclusive evidence establishing either person’s involvement has been presented.
Nevertheless, the development has opened another line of inquiry in a case that has remained unresolved since February 2012 despite repeated investigations and more than 130 missed deadlines for submitting a report.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Sikdar Mahmudur Razi and Justice Fatema Anwar on Tuesday granted the task force another six months to complete its investigation, setting April 29, 2027, as the next deadline.
The court also directed International Crimes Tribunal prosecutor Tanvir Hasan Joha to appear on that date and explain the information uncovered during the separate investigation.
According to Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal, the court will hear Joha in a closed-door session because of the sensitive nature of the information.
The latest development centres on information gathered by the International Crimes Tribunal’s prosecution while examining allegations involving Ziaul Ahsan, a former senior military intelligence officer.
The task force’s progress report refers to discussions with the tribunal’s Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam and prosecutor Tanvir Hasan Joha, during which preliminary information emerged concerning two individuals.
The report indicates that further investigation is necessary to establish whether the information has any connection to the murders and whether other people may have been involved.
The attorney general said approximately 300 discs had been recovered during a search linked to Ziaul’s residence in Barisal.
The materials are believed to contain different forms of digital information, potentially including audio and video recordings, conversations and other records.
Investigators have reviewed 90 discs, leaving another 210 to be examined.
What the discs contain, whether any of the material relates directly to Sagar and Runi’s deaths, and whether it can be used as evidence in the murder case have yet to be established.
The attorney general said the task force had formally requested relevant materials from the tribunal’s prosecution so that the investigating officer could examine them independently.
He stressed that information gathered during another investigation could not automatically be treated as established evidence in the Sagar-Runi case.
Earlier reporting had raised questions about possible connections involving Ziaul Ahsan and Rokeya Prachy. However, the precise nature of those connections remains under investigation.
Neither the emergence of their names nor the discovery of digital materials establishes criminal responsibility.
Court seeks answers directly from prosecutor
The High Court’s decision to hear Joha directly marks a significant step in assessing the new information.
According to the attorney general, the court wants to understand what was discovered, how the information was obtained and its possible relevance to the murder investigation.
The hearing will take place behind closed doors, rather than in open court.
The court did not separately summon the task force chief, with the attorney general saying the official regularly attends hearings in the case.
Lawyer Mohammad Shishir Monir, representing the complainant’s family, said the state had sought another year to complete the investigation.
The court instead granted six months.
He questioned why examining the remaining discs should require such a lengthy extension and urged the authorities to complete the investigation without further delay.
The task force must now verify the material obtained from the tribunal and determine whether it provides credible evidence capable of advancing the murder investigation.
Sagar Sarowar, news editor at Maasranga Television, and his wife Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were murdered at their rented apartment in West Rajabazar on February 11, 2012.
Their young son, Mahir Sarowar Megh, was at home at the time.
Runi’s brother, Nowsher Alam Roman, filed a murder case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station the following day.
The investigation was initially handled by police before being transferred to the Detective Branch and later to the Rapid Action Battalion.
RAB investigated the case for more than 12 years without submitting a final report.
On September 30, 2024, the High Court removed RAB from the investigation and ordered the formation of a high-powered task force under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
The government subsequently formed a four-member team headed by the chief of the Police Bureau of Investigation, with representatives from other law enforcement agencies.
Despite repeated extensions, the task force has yet to submit a conclusive report.
A Dhaka court deferred the investigation report for the 130th time on September 30 this year, setting November 5 as the next date for submission in the criminal proceedings.
The High Court’s latest order gives investigators another six months to examine the new information and report their findings.

item.title: Bhatara raid: 85 jailed, but was justice served?
item.description:
The imprisonment of 85 people following a police raid on a senior police officer’s house in Dhaka has raised serious questions about the fairness of the summary proceedings, with lawyers and human rights advocates demanding to know whether each detainee was given a proper opportunity to defend themselves.
The controversy has deepened after the seizure list from the Bhatara raid recorded just one yaba tablet, several bottles of liquor, drug-consumption paraphernalia and a small quantity of a substance identified as kush -- far less than the substantial drug recovery initially described by police.
The central question is no longer simply what happened inside the house, but what evidence was used to establish an offence against each of the 85 people who were subsequently jailed.
Barrister Sara Hossain told Dhaka Tribune that a human rights violation had “certainly” occurred.
Legal experts have questioned whether the detainees were allowed to consult lawyers, whether individual allegations were examined and whether the proceedings met the safeguards required by law.
Article 33 of the Constitution guarantees an arrested person the right to consult and be defended by a lawyer of their choice.
Yet the available account does not identify the specific offence established against each detainee, whether individual admissions were recorded or what evidence was considered before sentences were imposed.
The identities of the presiding magistrates, the legal provisions invoked and the individual conviction orders have also not been made public.
Detectives detained 85 people, including 26 women, during the raid on a house owned by Additional Deputy Inspector General Abdullah Al Zahir.
The men were sentenced to one month in jail and fined Tk1,000 each, with an additional 15 days’ imprisonment for non-payment.
The women received 15-day jail terms and Tk500 fines, with another three days in default of payment.
According to the seizure list, police recovered an empty 750ml bottle of Carew’s whisky, approximately 500ml of Royal Stag whisky, around 200ml of Smirnoff vodka and another bottle of Indian whisky.
The inventory also included one yaba tablet, paraphernalia used to consume the drug and a small quantity of kush.
Earlier, Detective Branch officials had claimed that large quantities of liquor, cannabis, yaba and other drugs had been recovered.
Several detectives acknowledged that the limited seizure was surprising given the number of people detained and the allegations of prolonged drug-related activities at the property.
Deputy Commissioner Elias Kabir of the DB’s Uttara division, who led the operation, said the detainees had consumed liquor and yaba before police arrived, leaving relatively little to be recovered.
However, the seizure of one tablet does not, by itself, establish possession or consumption by every person present.
Lawyers argue that attendance at a private gathering cannot automatically be treated as proof of an offence. Any allegation of illegal possession or consumption must be established against the individual concerned.
The summary nature of the proceedings has brought the detainees’ legal protections under scrutiny.
Rights advocates say the authorities must explain whether the accused were informed of the allegations against them, allowed access to legal counsel and given an opportunity to respond.
The legal basis for imposing different sentences on men and women also remains unclear from the available information.
Advocate Shahdeen Malik told Dhaka Tribune that human rights violations do not always provide a straightforward route to legal remedies under Bangladesh’s existing legal framework.
“Even if there has been a human rights violation, has any law been violated?” he asked, questioning the effectiveness of existing mechanisms for obtaining redress.
He noted that the National Human Rights Commission cannot itself impose criminal punishment or issue binding judicial decrees.
Under its governing legislation, the commission may investigate complaints, seek reconciliation and recommend legal action or compensation.
Malik said that where a rights violation also constitutes a criminal offence, including unlawful detention or physical torture, legal action may be pursued through the ordinary criminal justice system.
The distinction makes the circumstances of the convictions particularly important: the legality of the proceedings depends on the powers exercised, the offences alleged and whether the required procedures were followed.
The raid has also prompted questions about the use of the property owned by Additional DIG Zahir.
Kabir said five of the house’s six rooms were rented through online booking platforms, while the sixth was occupied by a caretaker.
According to police, the property was rented for Tk18,500 a day, with additional guests paying Tk600 each. Investigators alleged that 20 to 22 parties were held there every month.
Kabir claimed that Mahbubul Alam, who managed the arrangements, received 30% of the earnings, while Zahir received the remaining 70%.
Zahir has denied organising drug parties.
He told other news outlets that the property was rented for birthdays and other private functions, with rules prohibiting illegal activities. He maintained that the money he received was rental income and said he had been misled about the number of people attending.
Following the raid, he was removed from his previous assignment in the Maintenance and Repair branch and attached to Police Headquarters.
No finding of criminal responsibility against the officer has been established in the information available.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir: PM prioritises Bangladesh’s interests in ties with Japan
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has emphasized Bangladesh’s national interests in strengthening ties with Japan, prioritising development projects and investment that can create jobs, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday.
Briefing reporters at the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo after the prime minister’s bilateral summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Kobir said the talks focused on boosting trade, investment and economic cooperation and advancing strategic projects.
He said Japan’s private sector plans to invest around $6.34 billion in Bangladesh over the next five years, potentially creating employment opportunities for about 200,000 people.
The state minister said Tarique stressed the need for giving priority to investment in industries capable of generating jobs, as the government seeks to turn growing international interest in Bangladesh into concrete investment.
He said the two countries also discussed expediting the implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), which was signed in February 2026.
The prime minister sought Japan’s support to ensure a smooth and sustainable graduation of Bangladesh from the least developed country (LDC) category, Kobir said.
Bangladesh sought an additional three years to prepare for LDC graduation, citing the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, long-standing economic challenges and the recent global energy crisis, he said.
The state minister said Bangladesh urged Japan to give serious consideration to the request.
He said the two sides also discussed establishing a ministerial-level joint mechanism to accelerate bilateral cooperation, identify priority sectors, set specific timelines and regularly review progress.
Kobir said Japan showed interest in projects involving investment in Bangladesh’s energy sector, the development of a technology-based industrial city and infrastructure, including elevated expressways.
He also referred to Japanese development assistance worth 50 billion yen, equivalent to around $340 million.
Describing the visit as important for creating new investment opportunities and strengthening economic ties, the state minister said international partners are showing renewed interest in Bangladesh following the formation of its new democratically elected government.
He said one of the main objectives of the visit is to translate that interest into actual investment.
The prime minister’s visits to Japanese energy infrastructure and logistics facilities also offered opportunities to learn from Japan’s experience, particularly in LNG terminal development and modern logistics management, Kobir added.
Replying to a question about employment opportunities for Bangladeshi students and workers in Japan, he said the two countries are discussing Japanese-language training and the development of skilled manpower, with a process already at the implementation stage.
On the Rohingya crisis, the state minister said Bangladesh plans to raise the issue prominently in multilateral diplomatic forums next year and hopes for a positive role from Japan.
He described the prime minister’s visit as fruitful, saying the constructive discussions between the two leaders opened up new possibilities for Bangladesh’s development, industrialisation and job creation.
Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon and Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin were also present at the briefing.

item.title: Police Service Association calls IGP's crossfire remark a 'timely call'
item.description:
The Bangladesh Police Service Association (BPSA) has described Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir’s remarks on “crossfire” as a “timely call,” saying they should be viewed in the context of existing laws and regulations.
In a statement issued on Tuesday, the association said the remarks highlighted the need for proper implementation of the law, protection of public safety, and ensuring police personnel have the confidence and capacity to perform their duties.
The statement was signed by BPSA General Secretary Shamima Parvin, who is also superintendent of police in Dhaka district.
It said police personnel were facing various obstacles in enforcing the law and ensuring public safety amid the changing law-and-order situation, a growing mob culture and the post-August 5, 2024, political context.
The association said the IGP made the remarks at the inauguration of a community bank in Chawkbazar, Old Dhaka, and that they should be considered in light of existing laws and regulations.
According to the statement, the remarks underscored the need to take appropriate action as circumstances demand, within the limits of the law, while ensuring police personnel have the confidence and capacity to carry out their professional responsibilities.
The statement added that Bangladesh Police conducts all its activities in accordance with the constitution and prevailing laws.
Citing statistics on attacks against police personnel, the BPSA said 176 attacks on officers on duty were recorded in the first 10 months of 2026, leaving four police members dead and 370 seriously injured.
The association said the figures highlighted the need to ensure police personnel’s safety and provide them with a suitable working environment.
It added that officers must be able to perform their duties fearlessly, impartially and professionally, in accordance with the law, including the right of private defence.
The statement also said the association believed that maintaining strong law and order was essential to state stability and the uninterrupted continuation of economic activities.
It said the public expected police to protect life and property, suppress crime, uphold justice, and ensure impartiality and accountability. Police personnel must therefore perform their duties firmly, professionally and humanely, without hesitation in the lawful exercise of their authority.
The association warned that undue hesitation in exercising legal powers to combat crime could embolden criminals and undermine law and order, as well as the effectiveness of state institutions.
At the same time, it said police must operate within the limits of the law, maintaining firmness, impartiality and professionalism to strengthen public trust.
The BPSA said the IGP’s remarks could therefore be viewed as a timely call for the proper and firm enforcement of existing laws, effective crime suppression and stronger police capacity to protect public safety.

item.title: Rumon: Tarique Rahman, Takaichi hold fruitful bilateral talks
item.description:
The bilateral meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi was fruitful, said Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.
Briefing reporters at the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo on Tuesday night, Rumon said the Bangladesh premier attended an official luncheon after the meeting and later visited various Japanese institutions and facilities.
He said Tarique Rahman visited different industrial establishments and facilities in Japan to explore how the country’s experience could be utilized for Bangladesh’s development and industrialization.
The prime minister is visiting Japan with a focus on Bangladesh’s development, Rumon said, adding that the government is working to make the country’s economy and institutions more efficient while creating new opportunities for industrialization.
“The main purpose of visiting various industrial establishments and facilities in Japan is to learn about their operations and experience and assess how these can be utilised for Bangladesh’s development,” he said.
Rumon added that the prime minister was undertaking various initiatives to ensure the welfare and development of the people, and the programmes during his Japan visit had been designed to expand Bangladesh’s development prospects.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir and Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin were also present at the press conference.

item.title: Kurigram road crash: Mother dies with unborn child a day after daughter’s death
item.description:
A mother and her unborn child died from injuries sustained in a bus crash in Kurigram, a day after the accident claimed the life of her six-year-old daughter.
Aduri Bala, 23, died while undergoing treatment at Rangpur Medical College Hospital on Tuesday morning, her father-in-law Dulal Chandra Mali confirmed the matter.
The accident occurred around 8:30pm on Monday near Kathalbari Bazar in Kurigram Sadar.
Aduri’s six-year-old daughter, Monika Mali, was killed when a Dhaka-bound bus of Pingki Paribahan hit the autorickshaw carrying the family.
Aduri, her husband Ananta Mali, 26, and the autorickshaw driver, Mozammel, 29, were seriously injured in the crash.
Aduri and Ananta were taken to Rangpur Medical College Hospital that night for advanced treatment. Aduri died there the following morning. She was seven months pregnant.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune from Kurigram General Hospital on Monday night, Ananta said he was returning home to Trimohoni in Kurigram Sadar with his wife and daughter after visiting his in-laws in Kulaghat, Lalmonirhat.
“Near Kathalbari, a Dhaka-bound Pingki Paribahan bus hit our autorickshaw, throwing us onto the road. Local residents rescued us and took us to hospital,” he said.
Dulal Chandra Mali said: “My granddaughter died last night, and my daughter-in-law Aduri, who was seven months pregnant, died this morning. My son is also in critical condition. We have lost everything. I don’t know where to seek justice or whether we will be able to file a case.”
Kamal Hossain, officer-in-charge of Kurigram Sadar Police Station, said that legal proceedings are underway in connection with the casualties in the accident.

item.title: Tongi madrasa case: Rumi still in Bangladesh, seeks High Court bail
item.description:
Shahjalal Rumi, the father of a seven-year-old child allegedly sexually abused at a madrasa in Tongi, Gazipur, remains in Bangladesh and has sought anticipatory bail from the High Court in a counter-case accusing him of assault, attempted murder and theft. Rumi’s lawyer, HM Ruhul Amin Mollah (Hasan), confirmed the matter on Tuesday.
He said Rumi had spent several hours at his chamber from Monday afternoon seeking legal assistance. An anticipatory bail petition has been filed with the High Court in connection with the case lodged against him with Tongi West Police Station. The hearing date has yet to be fixed.
The lawyer said his client respects the law and trusts the judicial system, adding that Rumi wants to ensure his and his family’s safety and seek justice through legal means.
On October 21, a seven-year-old student was allegedly sexually abused at Qariul Quran International Cadet Madrasa in Tongi’s Auchpara area. Following the allegation, the child’s father assaulted the accused teacher, Md Moslem Uddin, who was later handed over to police.
A video of the incident went viral on social media, sparking widespread debate and criticism. Rumi subsequently filed a case over the alleged sexual abuse with Tongi West Police Station.
In a counter-case filed on behalf of the madrasa’s principal, Rumi was accused of stealing Tk17 lakh, assault and attempted murder. He had not been seen in public since the case was filed.
On Monday night, Rumi told journalists that he had left the country.
“I am no longer in this country. I am not thinking about these matters anymore. Whatever happens, let it happen. You all stay well,” he said.
However, according to his lawyer, Rumi is still in Bangladesh and has sought legal protection through an anticipatory bail petition before the High Court.

item.title: Woman robbed of Tk25 lakh at gunpoint in Chittagong's Raozan
item.description:
A woman has alleged that a group of armed men robbed her of Tk25 lakh at gunpoint in broad daylight in Raozan, Chittagong, on Tuesday.
The incident took place around 10:30am in the Baruapara area when the woman was travelling to a sub-registry office to register a land purchase.
The victim, Shamsun Nahar, a resident of Ward 8 of Kadolpur union, said eight to 10 armed men travelling on two motorcycles and a CNG-run autorickshaw were involved in the robbery.
She was carrying Tk25 lakh in cash to the sub-registry office to complete the land registration.
Shamsun said a motorcycle blocked the auto-rickshaw's path. Two men got off another motorcycle, took the vehicle's keys and seized the driver's mobile phone.
When the driver tried to resist, one of the men pulled out a pistol. Two more men arriving on another motorcycle then threatened Shamsun at gunpoint and snatched her bag containing the money.
“I told them to kill me if they wanted, but not to take my money. But they took it anyway. It was money my younger son had saved through a lot of hardship. I was going to buy land with his savings. I don't know what I will do now,” she said.
The incident has sparked concern across Raozan.
Barrister Tarek Akbar Khondaker, convener of the central executive committee of the Khaleda Zia Smriti Sangsad, condemned the robbery and expressed concern over the law and order situation in the upazila.
“Such incidents are in no way acceptable,” he said, urging the administration to ensure the safety of people's lives and property.
Raozan police station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Islam told Dhaka Tribune that Shamsun had filed a general diary (GD) with the police.
“Efforts are underway to identify those involved in the robbery and bring them to justice,” he said.
A series of violent incidents, shootings and murders in Raozan in recent months has heightened public concern. At least 12 criminal groups are active across the upazila's 14 unions and one municipality.
Nurul Amin, a trader at Pahartali Chowmuhani Market, said even betel-leaf sellers had to pay extortion money to run their businesses.
According to law enforcement agencies, 27 murders were recorded in the upazila between August 5, 2024, and September 2026. Police said 20 of the killings were linked to political rivalries.

item.title: Police ordered to crack down on drug, juvenile gang kingpins
item.description:
Additional Inspector General of Police (Crime and Operations) Md Sayedur Rahman has directed police to identify and take strict action against kingpins involved in drug trafficking and juvenile gangs.
He issued the directive while presiding over the monthly crime review meeting at Police Headquarters on Tuesday afternoon.
Metropolitan police commissioners, range deputy inspectors general (DIGs) and district superintendents of police (SPs) joined the meeting virtually. DIG (Crime Management) Mohammad Abu Sufian and other senior officials attended in person.
Sayedur Rahman said Bangladesh Police maintains a “zero-tolerance” policy towards drugs and juvenile gangs.
He urged field-level police personnel to perform their duties with honesty, dedication and professionalism to improve the force’s public image. He also stressed the need for humane treatment of the public.
The additional IGP instructed police to register robbery cases promptly and expedite investigations to bring perpetrators to justice.
Emphasising close supervision of rape investigations, he said it would help increase the conviction rate. He also directed police officials to improve the rate of disposal of other cases.

item.title: BSCIC observes World Iodine Day 2026
item.description:
The Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation (BSCIC) organized a discussion meeting titled "importance of iodine in building an intelligent nation" at its headquarters at Tejgaon in the capital on Tuesday, marking World Iodine Day 2026.
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit attended the program as the chief guest. BSCIC Chairman Benzir Ahmed chaired the meeting, while Industries Secretary Abdun Naser Khan attended the program as the special guest.
Other special guests included Dr Rudaba Khondker, country director of GAIN Bangladesh, Dr AKM Musha, country director of NI Bangladesh, and Nurul Kabir, president of Bangladesh Salt Mill Owners Association.
Professor Dr Mohammad Gulzarul Aziz of Bangladesh Agricultural University delivered a presentation on the importance of iodine in building an intelligent nation.

item.title: South Korean delegation meets JU VC
item.description:
A delegation led by Professor Choi Hae-Young, an emeritus professor at Chonnam National University in South Korea, paid a courtesy call on Jahangirnagar University (JU) Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Nurul Islam on Tuesday.
The meeting took place at 3;00pm in the vice-chancellor’s office.
Professor Ahmed Reza of JU’s Department of English, South Korean national and language instructor Lee Ku and his wife, Lee Charles, were also present.
During the meeting, the vice-chancellor expressed interest in strengthening cooperation between Bangladesh and South Korea in education and research, including exchanges of students and faculty members.
Professor Choi Hae-Young stressed the importance of continuing discussions to further strengthen mutual cooperation.

item.title: Activists demand national ownership of energy master plan
item.description:
Environmental and energy-sector activists in Rajshahi have called for national ownership, public participation and energy sovereignty in formulating Bangladesh’s energy master plan, stressing that the process must remain under the leadership and decision-making authority of national institutions.
The demand was raised on Tuesday at a campaign titled ‘Energy Master Plan: No to Japan, No to Foreigners! The Nation Must Participate in Its Own Plan’.
The organisers said Bangladesh needed an independent, transparent and people-centred energy master plan based on its own needs and capabilities to address dependence on imported fossil fuels, rising energy costs, pressure on foreign exchange reserves and climate change risks.
They called for the public disclosure of the draft plan, energy demand forecasts, financial assessments, and environmental and social impact assessments to ensure transparency in the planning process.
They also stressed the need for public consultations at both national and local levels to ensure meaningful participation by domestic experts, universities, civil society organisations and communities affected by energy projects.
The organisers urged the government to reduce dependence on imported energy and prioritise renewable energy, rooftop solar power, energy efficiency and an environmentally sustainable transition.
They said transparency and accountability in formulating the master plan would help safeguard national interests and strengthen public confidence in energy-sector policies.
Those present at the programme included Paribartan COP Facilitator Hasibul Hasan Pallab, Campaign Associate Rony Roy, agricultural entrepreneur Liaquat Ali, Programme Officer Soma Bhowmik and Paribartan intern Sabitri Hembram. Local residents also attended the event and expressed solidarity with the initiative.
The organisers reiterated that public opinion and participation must be central to decisions shaping Bangladesh’s energy future. They called for an energy master plan that prioritises national interests, transparency and accountability.
The initiative was organised by Paribartan, FED-Rajshahi and the Bangladesh Working Group on Ecology and Development (BWGED).

item.title: Jamaat challenges Rashed to prove allegation of Porwar’s meeting with Indian intelligence official
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has challenged Prime Minister’s Special Assistant Mohammad Rashed Khan to prove his allegation that the party’s secretary general, Mia Golam Porwar, held a secret meeting with a senior Indian intelligence official.

In response to the allegation, Jamaat also said it had doubts about the mental and political soundness of those spreading such false information.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the party strongly condemned and protested reports published in various media outlets alleging that Porwar had met an intelligence agency from a foreign country.

Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair, secretary of Jamaat’s publicity and media department, said in the statement that the party conducted its political activities through constitutional means and maintained diplomatic relations with foreign countries while upholding the dignity of the state.

However, he said, reports had recently appeared in various media outlets claiming that Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar had met an intelligence agency from a foreign country in what the party described as a conspiracy to tarnish its reputation.

The statement urged the country’s media outlets to verify the accuracy of the information and the truth of the allegations before publishing reports on matters of national importance. It also called on citizens to remain alert to false information and propaganda and not to be misled.

Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair challenged those who had circulated what he called false information about Jamaat’s secretary general to prove their claims.

“They should disclose the truth of the allegations before the nation,” he said, adding that attempts to discredit the party’s secretary general through false information would not succeed.

On Monday, Rashed Khan wrote in a Facebook post that Porwar, Jamaat leader ATM Masum and one other person had met a senior Indian intelligence official at a house in Baridhara, Dhaka on 16 September.

“Those who speak against India throughout the day—why, and in whose interests, did they take part in a secret meeting with this Indian intelligence official? Meeting an Indian diplomat and meeting a senior Indian intelligence official are not the same thing,” Rashed wrote in his post.

The prime minister’s special assistant further wrote, “If Mia Golam Porwar practises ethical politics, I hope he will clarify the details of this secret meeting. Otherwise, it will have to be assumed that Jamaat is involved in a deep conspiracy against the state.”

He added that the first step in the conspiracy was a plan by Jamaat to launch a movement alongside the Awami League.

item.title: Zubaida Rahman urges Sasakawa Foundation to expand health cooperation in Bangladesh
item.description:
Zubaida Rahman, wife of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, called upon the Sasakawa Peace Foundation to expand its cooperation with Bangladesh in healthcare, medical research, maternal and child health, and the development of modern medical infrastructure.

She made the call while addressing a health-related seminar organised by the Sasakawa Peace Foundation in Tokyo this afternoon (local time).

Zubaida said, “The present government of Bangladesh has identified healthcare, education and social protection as major policy priorities."

The government had undertaken various initiatives to ensure affordable healthcare for all, improve the quality of public health services, recruit healthcare workers and expand access to health and education for disadvantaged communities, she added.

She said the government was also working to improve people's living standards through employment-oriented education, greater educational opportunities for underprivileged students, family-based social assistance programmes and the introduction of Family Card.

Describing health as an important area of her professional and personal interest, Zubaida said ensuring people's physical and mental well-being was crucial.

“Bangladesh-Japan bilateral relations are continuously evolving. There are opportunities to address emerging challenges in the health and social sectors by utilising the experience, knowledge and capacities of both countries,” she said.

Emphasising the shared commitment of Bangladesh and Japan to ensuring a healthy environment for children to grow up and realise their full potential, she said sustainable social systems, strong economies, quality education and protection against violence, poverty and other risks were essential to achieving the goal.

Highlighting the importance of health diplomacy amid growing global interconnectedness, she said it could play a significant role in achieving the common goal of ensuring health for all.

Zubaida also stressed the contributions of non-governmental organisations, international institutions, voluntary initiatives and philanthropic foundations, alongside government efforts, to improving maternal and child health in Bangladesh.

Referring to her professional experience as a physician in Bangladesh, she said the country had considerable potential to implement appropriate health policies, advance medical research and establish modern healthcare institutions.

Appreciating the Sasakawa Peace Foundation’s efforts to protect the health of children and vulnerable communities, she called for expanding its activities in Bangladesh and urged the foundation to extend greater resources and cooperation to address the country's health challenges.

She said the Bangladesh government was ready to extend full cooperation and support to initiatives aimed at protecting and promoting health and ensuring sustainable healthcare services in the long term.

Honorary Chairman of the Nippon Foundation and the Sasakawa Peace Foundation Yohei Sasakawa and other distinguished guests attended the seminar.

item.title: IGP should step down as soon as possible: Nahid Islam
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam has said Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir should step down over his remarks about “crossfire”. He has also called for reforms to the police force.

Speaking at a meeting organised by the NCP in Gazipur on Tuesday afternoon, Nahid Islam said, “We believe that apologising is not enough; the IGP no longer has the right to remain in office. We have demanded his removal. He should step down as soon as possible.

As the head of a law enforcement agency, he was supposed to ensure the rule of law, yet he has said he would carry out crossfire killings if the government instructed him to do so. We did not even see anyone speak so openly about this during Sheikh Hasina’s tenure. Therefore, the police force must certainly undergo reforms.”

On Monday, IGP Md Ali Hossain Fakir said at an event in Chawkbazar in Old Dhaka that the police would carry out “crossfire” (extrajudicial killings) if the government gave permission and the situation required it.

Speaking about local government elections, Nahid Islam said BNP leaders were establishing their dominance at the grassroots level. He warned that the government and the Election Commission would fail if they could not ensure free and fair elections.

He also threatened to take to the streets if the authorities conducted elections through partisan control, as the previous government had done.

Nahid Islam further alleged that the government was gradually becoming authoritarian, like the Awami League. He said BNP loyalists were being placed in administrative positions, the police chief was threatening crossfire killings, and authorities were filing cases under anti-terrorism laws against people who criticised the government. He also accused the government of politicising the administration, saying that holding elections under such circumstances would be difficult.

The NCP convener also criticised the government for increasing the salaries of public sector employees while leaving garment workers’ wages unchanged. He expressed support for the demand to raise the minimum monthly wage for garment workers to Tk 30,000.

The NCP organised the meeting at the district council auditorium to review the party’s organisational progress and formulate central plans for the local government elections.

Those present included NCP political council member and Senior Joint Member Secretary Sarjis Alam; Joint Convener and political council member Ali Ahsan Zonaed; Dhaka North Organising Secretary Saifullah Hyder; and leaders from the district and upazila levels in Gazipur.

Later, at around 8.30 pm on Tuesday, Nahid Islam visited Md Bappi at Beraiderchala in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur. Bappi became physically disabled during the July uprising.

Speaking to journalists there, Nahid Islam said, “This government is the outcome of the July mass uprising. This election became possible, and the government was able to assume power, because hundreds of people sacrificed their lives, lost limbs or became physically disabled. The government must give these injured brothers and sisters due attention, putting politics and everything else aside. Their treatment must not suffer because of administrative or bureaucratic complications.”
